rules.action: Scoring balloon first-line. Escalate to IVL if residual waist persists after scoring.
Scoring or cutting balloon first; escalate to IVL before stenting if waist persists — do not proceed with persistent non-compliance.
Plan calcium modification before the case. Short atherectomy bursts (<30s). Confirm full balloon compliance before stenting.

Assess calcium depth and distribution with intravascular imaging before selecting modification device. IVL for deep/medial calcium and nodules; RA for superficial calcium and balloon-uncrossable lesions.
RA followed by IVL (Dual-Prep) is a reasonable escalation when post-atherectomy imaging reveals persistent heavy calcification.
Plan calcium modification before the case. Short RA bursts (<30s) with adequate flushing. Consider staged debulking if diffuse.
IVL preferred over RA at the ostium. Disengage guide during IVL pulses to avoid aortic root energy transmission.
rules.caution: Do not inflate IVL balloon with guide deeply engaged at the ostium.

rules.action: Use short marker-to-marker stent. Disengage guide 1–2mm before final deployment. Post-dilate with NC balloon flared at the ostium.
Plan stent overlap zones before deploying. Deploy distal stent first, work proximally. Post-dilate each segment before deploying the next.
rules.caution: Avoid geographic miss at proximal or distal edges — high risk of edge restenosis.

rules.action: Intravascular imaging mandatory before stenting. Deploy stents distal to proximal with ≥3mm overlap zones. Post-dilate each segment before deploying the next.
Restore antegrade flow before stenting where possible. Staged approach (aspiration → reassess → definitive stenting) reduces no-reflow risk.
Aspiration thrombectomy first to restore flow; reassess true lesion before stenting. If TIMI 0 persists after aspiration, consider pharmacoinvasive strategy (GPI, deferred PCI 24–48h).
Aspiration thrombectomy recommended before balloon or stent delivery. If high residual burden persists, consider deferred stenting (24–48h with anticoagulation and GPI).
Avoid aspiration thrombectomy. EPD mandatory. Consider pharmacoinvasive approach (GP IIb/IIIa) before definitive stenting. Direct stenting preferred over pre-dilation.
rules.caution: Aspiration in a thrombosed degenerated SVG carries high no-reflow risk.

rules.action: Avoid aspiration thrombectomy. EPD as standard. Pre-treat with GP IIb/IIIa. Direct stenting preferred over pre-dilation where anatomy permits.

Avoid pre-dilation unless lesion is severely stenotic or EPD delivery requires it. Direct stenting preferred. Slow nominal-pressure inflations. Avoid post-dilatation; if required, size 1:1 — never oversize.
EPD whenever technically feasible. Intracoronary vasodilators (verapamil, adenosine, nitroprusside) liberally — even before balloon or stenting, delivered distally via microcatheter or OTW balloon.
Dedicated aspiration catheters or guide extension aspiration for moderate burden; mechanical thrombectomy (AngioJet, Penumbra) for very large thrombus. Maintain high ACT throughout.
rules.caution: Limited RCT evidence for SVG thrombectomy devices.

rules.action: Keep atherectomy bursts and balloon inflations short (<30s). Vasopressors immediately available. Consider staged procedure if haemodynamic reserve is borderline.
Keep inflation times short; deflate promptly if haemodynamics deteriorate. Staged procedure is a reasonable strategy for high-complexity lesions.
Calcium modification must achieve full lesion compliance before stenting. Accept a longer procedure — do not rush preparation.
rules.caution: Do not stent until full balloon compliance is confirmed — no bailout exists if the result is inadequate.

rules.action: IVUS-guided sizing mandatory. Pre-dilate cautiously with vasopressors available. For LM shaft/ostial disease without bifurcation, single stent preferred. Ensure continuous haemodynamic monitoring.
